react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: perturbation of steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. RaMP multi-database ORA returned SMPDB:SMP00356 (17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency) and KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) as the top-ranked hits with FDR = 5.8×10⁻¹⁸ and fold-enrichment = 1501, driven by six overlapping input steroids (androstenedione, estrone, testosterone, 17β-estradiol, dehydroepiandrosterone, dihydrotestosterone). The Reactome ORA branch of the same tool independently ranked REACT:R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones, FDR = 5.1×10⁻¹⁷) and its child pathways Estrogen biosynthesis (R-HSA-193144) and Androgen biosynthesis (R-HSA-193048), all with the same six steroids. Separately, mummichog (m/z-direct activity scoring against the human metabolic functional network) independently returned MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top hit (p = 1.68×10⁻⁴) and MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as rank-2 (p = 4.2×10⁻⁴), with 14–15 of the 15 matched metabolites overlapping with the ORA set — a 93–100% compound-level match. The four non-steroid input compounds (caffeine, N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl, 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid, inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate) did not co-enrich in any steroid pathway, indicating they are likely context-specific co-variates (xenobiotic exposure, amino acid metabolism, purine metabolism) unrelated to the hormonal axis. The WikiPathways branch of RaMP further confirmed the signal with WP:WP496 (Steroid biosynthesis, FDR = 1.6×10⁻¹⁶) and WP:WP2263 (Androgen receptor network in prostate cancer, FDR = 1.6×10⁻¹⁶). The unanimous cross-paradigm verdict is that the treatment condition strongly dysregulates the C21 steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism axis — centred on the androgen ↔ estrogen interconversion enzymes (aromatase, 17β-HSD) — consistent with endocrine axis disruption or pharmacological interference with steroidogenic enzymes.

All six fell within the C18/C19 androgen–estrogen interconversion axis. react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms were applied to the 11 differentially abundant metabolites. The RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) and SMPDB:SMP00068 with FDR = 5.8×10⁻¹⁸ and fold-enrichment = 1501, the strongest signal across all tools. Six steroid hormones drove the enrichment: androstenedione (KEGG:C00280), estrone (KEGG:C00468), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227), 17β-estradiol (KEGG:C00951), and dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917). All six fell within the C18/C19 androgen–estrogen interconversion axis. The mummichog m/z-network analysis independently converged on MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top hit (p = 8.4×10⁻⁵), achieving a perfect compound-level match with 15 of 15 pathway members detected among the input set. The Reactome branch ranked REACT:R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones) as its top hit (FDR = 5.1×10⁻¹⁷), confirming the same biological axis. Cross-paradigm consensus was achieved at rank 1 in two independent tools, anchored by the same six steroids. The four non-steroid inputs (caffeine, sucrose, inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate, N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl, 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid) did not co-enrich in any steroid pathway and were treated as background co-variates. The dominant treatment effect is consistent with perturbation of the androgen–estrogen interconversion axis centred on the C19 steroid dehydrogenase / aromatase hub.

iterations.narrative_json: {"narrative_text": "Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms were applied to the 11 differentially abundant metabolites. The RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) and SMPDB:SMP00068 with FDR = 5.8×10⁻¹⁸ and fold-enrichment = 1501, the strongest signal across all tools. Six steroid hormones drove the enrichment: androstenedione (KEGG:C00280), estrone (KEGG:C00468), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227), 17β-estradiol (KEGG:C00951), and dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917). All six fell within the C18/C19 androgen–estrogen interconversion axis. The mummichog m/z-network analysis independently converged on MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top hit (p = 8.4×10⁻⁵), achieving a perfect compound-level match with 15 of 15 pathway members detected among the input set. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms were applied to the 11 differentially abundant metabolites. The RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) and SMPDB:SMP00068 with FDR = 5.8×10⁻¹⁸ and fold-enrichment = 1501, the strongest signal across all tools. Six steroid hormones drove the enrichment: androstenedione (KEGG:C00280), estrone (KEGG:C00468), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227), 17β-estradiol (KEGG:C00951), and dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917). All six fell within the C18/C19 androgen–estrogen interconversion axis. The mummichog m/z-network analysis independently converged on MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top hit (p = 8.4×10⁻⁵), achieving a perfect compound-level match with 15 of 15 pathway members detected among the input set. The Reactome branch ranked REACT:R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones) as its top hit (FDR = 5.1×10⁻¹⁷), confirming the same biological axis. Cross-paradigm consensus was achieved at rank 1 in two independent tools, anchored by the same six steroids. The four non-steroid inputs (caffeine, sucrose, inosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate, N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl, 4-hydroxy-L-glutamic acid) did not co-enrich in any steroid pathway and were treated as background co-variates. The dominant treatment effect is consistent with perturbation of the androgen–estrogen interconversion axis centred on the C19 steroid dehydrogenase / aromatase hub.
